svg.text: COST vs STURDINESS — plate gauge x MM-C-32 count, live prices, cutoffs drawn

Each cell: plate (bent, black powder coat, SendCutSend 2026-09-08) + magnets at the 5-9 break. Row = how much the screen edge moves under a 5 lb press; column = how hard a bump must push to slide the mount.
Red lines are the cutoffs: feels rigid (< 0.2 mm) and bump margin (slide >= 30 lb). Grey rows cost more than 0.187 in steel and flex more — nothing to buy there. Green = chosen.
FEELS RIGID below this line (< 0.2 mm)
Cheapest viable cell: A36/1008 .104 in with 4 x MM-C-32 = $204.25 (flex 0.128 mm, slide 35 lb).
Chosen: A36/1008 .187 in with 8 x = $261.02. The extra $56.77 buys 6x less flex and 1.6x the slide resistance — margin against the 35 % magnet derate, which is the number nobody has measured.

Diminishing returns: every plate dearer than 0.187 in steel either flexes more (grey) or removes flex no finger can feel; every magnet past 8 needs holes the plate does not have. The chosen cell is the corner of the viable region, not the middle of it.
MY ORDER OF PREFERENCE — stiffest plate first ("I don't want the plate to be too flimsy"), then the most magnets, then cost. The numbers in the cells are this list.
A36/1008 .187 in — the only gauge whose flex is below anything a finger can find; hot-rolled, so it undercuts 0.135
1. 8 x MM-C-32 $261.02 flex 0.022 mm, slide 56 lb — full margin against both estimates
2. 6 x MM-C-32 $245.74 flex 0.022 mm, slide 46 lb — in the band, one estimate less margin
3. 4 x MM-C-32 $230.46 flex 0.022 mm, slide 35 lb — passes only because the rubber skin is credited — an estimate on an estimate
A36/1008 .119 in — fine on paper, 4x the flex of 0.187 for $13 less — not a trade worth making
4. 8 x MM-C-32 $248.32 flex 0.085 mm, slide 56 lb — full margin against both estimates
5. 6 x MM-C-32 $233.04 flex 0.085 mm, slide 46 lb — in the band, one estimate less margin
6. 4 x MM-C-32 $217.76 flex 0.085 mm, slide 35 lb — passes only because the rubber skin is credited — an estimate on an estimate
A36/1008 .104 in — inside the rigid band by a third; the thinnest steel I would call not flimsy, and only just
7. 8 x MM-C-32 $234.81 flex 0.128 mm, slide 56 lb — full margin against both estimates
8. 6 x MM-C-32 $219.53 flex 0.128 mm, slide 46 lb — in the band, one estimate less margin
9. 4 x MM-C-32 $204.25 flex 0.128 mm, slide 35 lb — passes only because the rubber skin is credited — an estimate on an estimate
